findings.problem: "Come ___?" with cue stare and "How are you?" (en/ar do not mark register) accepts both stai and the polite sta, which the note itself gives; a learner typing sta would be marked wrong. Retarget to Come, which is unique.
"Di dove ___?" with cue essere accepts sei and the polite è ("Where are you from?" is register-neutral in en/ar). Retarget to dove, which is unique.
"Dove ___?" with cue abitare accepts abiti and the polite abita (given in the note); en/ar translations do not mark register. Retarget to Dove.
"___ un attimo." with cue aspettare accepts Aspetta and the polite Aspetti (given in the note); "Wait a moment." is register-neutral in en/vi/ar. Retarget to attimo; the cue then rules out momento.
"Sei ___?" with cue sicuro accepts sicuro and sicura ("Are you sure?" is gender-neutral in en/tr/fa/vi); blanking Sei instead would accept the polite È. No unique target, so drop the cloze.
"Mi sono ___." with cue perdersi accepts perso and persa ("I'm lost" has no gender in en/tr/fa/vi/es); the note gives persa. Retarget to the auxiliary sono, which is unique.
"È ___!" with cue buono accepts buonissimo, buonissima (note gives it for la pizza) and arguably plain buono for "It's delicious". Drop the cloze.
"Sono ___." with cue vegetariano accepts vegetariano and vegetariana ("I'm vegetarian" is gender-neutral in most translations); the note gives vegetariana. Retarget to Sono.
"Sono ___." with cue pieno accepts pieno and piena (given in the note); the translations do not fix gender. Retarget to Sono.
"Sono ___." with cue impegnato accepts impegnato and impegnata (given in the note); "I'm busy" is gender-neutral. Retarget to Sono.
"Sono ___." with cue stanco accepts stanco and stanca (given in the note); "I'm tired" is gender-neutral. Retarget to Sono.
"Sono ___." with cue malato accepts malato and malata (given in the note); "I'm sick" is gender-neutral. Retarget to Sono.
"È ___?" with cue aperto accepts aperto and aperta (the note gives È aperta? for la farmacia); "Is it open?" does not fix the gender of "it". Drop the cloze.
"È ___." with cue chiuso accepts chiuso and chiusa (the note gives È chiusa); "It's closed" does not fix the gender. Drop the cloze.

"È ___?" with cue lontano: lontana is equally correct when the referent is feminine ("La stazione è lontana?"), and "Is it far?" does not fix the gender of "it"; same issue as aperto/chiuso. Drop the cloze.
"Mi ___." with cue mancare: English "I miss you" can be plural, so mancate is also defensible for en learners. The other translations are singular.
The note overstates a rule: "Sì, per favore" is also used in Italian. Sì, grazie is just the more usual reply.

fix.note: Italians usually accept an offer with grazie rather than per favore.

rounds.summary: The Italian text, notes and all six translations are good: idiomatic A1 chunks, correct elisions and accents, registers and feminine variants noted properly, fa with ی/ک and ZWNJ, MSA with correct hamza. The weak spot is the cloze targets. 15 cards blank an inflected word whose tu/Lei or masculine/feminine alternative (often the very one the note gives) is equally valid for a translation that does not mark register or gender. Retargeting to a unique word fixes most of them. Clozes whose cue equals the answer (piano, dopo, favore) are not ambiguous under the cue rule.

newFindings.problem: Quello is "that" (es ese, en that), but "من هذا؟" means "who is this?". MSA distinguishes the two.
"برای بردن" is a calque of "to take away". The everyday Persian takeaway word is بیرون‌بر.
"Tôi đến đây để đi nghỉ" is awkward ("came here in order to go resting"). Natural Vietnamese for being here on holiday is "đến đây du lịch".
"Cho tôi dừng ở đây" ("let me stop here") misframes the request. A passenger tells a taxi driver "Cho tôi xuống ở đây" ("let me off here").
The bare fragment "Dümdüz ileri." sounds like a marching command. Directions in Turkish use a verb: "Dümdüz gidin."
"Hẹn gặp lại ngày mai!" (no "vào") reads as a calque. The everyday informal phrase is "Mai gặp lại nhé!"
"Tôi thích nó." is translationese: "nó" for an object is stilted. Natives say "Tôi thích cái này." or just "Thích lắm."
"Tôi không thích nó." has the same stilted "nó" as feelings-04.
"Nó ở đây." is grammatical but stiff. "Ở đây này." is the natural reply.
"مبروك" is universal but colloquial-leaning. Strict MSA prefers "تهانينا!".
"المعذرة" leans towards an apology. To get attention or pass by, "عذرًا" (or "لو سمحت") fits Mi scusi better.
"أيّ واحد؟" is grammatical but mirrors the colloquial. "أيّها؟" is the more idiomatic MSA.
"For late at night: stanotte" is unclear. Stanotte means the night just past (or tonight), not a time of day.

fix.note: For the night just past (after midnight): stanotte.
